zeal: The fervour or tireless devotion for a person, cause, or ideal and determination in its furtherance; diligent enthusiasm; powerful interest.
zealot: One who is zealous, one who is full of zeal for their own specific beliefs or objectives, usually in the negative sense of being too passionate; a fanatic.
zealotry: Something characteristic of a zealot; excessive zeal; fanaticism.
zealous: Full of zeal; ardent, fervent; exhibiting enthusiasm or strong passion, particularly in matters of religion.
zealously: Like, or in the manner of, a zealot; with great zeal or zealotry.
zealousness: The quality of being zealous; zeal.
zeatin: A plant hormone derived from adenine, having the chemical formula C₁₀H₁₃N₅O.
zebra: Any of three species of subgenus Hippotigris: Equus grevyi, Equus quagga, or Equus zebra, all with black and white stripes and native to Africa.
zebraic: Having a pattern of broken stripes.
zebrawood: Any wood with a figure (grain pattern) like the striping of a zebra, most often wood of the genus Microberlinia.
zebrine: Of, like, or pertaining to a zebra.
zebroid: A cross between a zebra and any other equine animal, but especially a horse.
zebu: A domesticated ox native to Asia and Africa, having a large fleshy hump on its back and a dewlap (Bos taurus indicus or bos indicus).
zecchin: Any of various gold coins produced in Italy or Turkey; a sequin.
zecchino: An old gold coin of Italy; a sequin.
zed: The name of the Latin script letter Z/z.
zedoary: Curcuma zedoaria, a perennial herb native to India and Indonesia.
zee: The name of the Latin script letter Z/z.
zein: A protein derived from corn/maize, having many industrial applications.
zeitgeber: A rhythmically occurring cue given by the environment, such as a change in light or temperature, to reset the internal body clock.
zeitgeist: The spirit of the age; the taste, outlook, and spirit characteristic of a period.
zek: A prisoner at a Russian prison, especially (historical) at a Soviet labour camp.
zelkova: A kind of tree in the elm family (genus Zelkova).
zemstvo: A Russian district or provincial council, or elective local-governmental administrative division, founded in 1864 by Tsar Alexander the Liberator.
zenana: Synonym of harem (“area of house or palace for high-caste women or wives of a wealthy man; the women thus kept; the system of segregating women in this way”).
zenith: The point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer; the point in the celestial sphere opposite the nadir.
zenithal: Of or pertaining to a zenith.

zeolitic: Of, pertaining to, containing, or produced using a zeolite.
zephyr: A light wind from the west.
zerk: Any of a class of types of grease nipples, or an instance thereof; (usually, in current usage) any grease nipple.
zero: The cardinal number occurring before one and that denotes no quantity or amount at all, represented in Arabic numerals as 0.
zeroed: simple past and past participle of zero.
zeroing: present participle and gerund of zero
zeroth: In the initial position in a sequence whose elements are numbered starting at zero; the ordinal number corresponding to zero.
zest: The outer skin of a citrus fruit, used as a flavouring or garnish.
zested: simple past and past participle of zest
zester: A kitchen implement used to remove the zest of citrus fruit.
zestfulness: State or condition of being zestful or enthusiastic.
zestier: comparative form of zesty: more zesty
zestiest: superlative form of zesty: most zesty
zesting: present participle and gerund of zest
zesty: Having a piquant or pungent taste; spicy.

zeugma: The act of using a word, particularly an adjective or verb, to apply to more than one noun when its sense is appropriate to only one.
